subject: Dominant species in two species co-occupancy model in MacKenzie et al. 2018

messages.author: 5d8084b4d758276c
messages.subject: Dominant species in two species co-occupancy model in MacKenzie et al. 2018
parts:
Hello, everyone. 

I'm reading the MacKenzie et al. 2018 book in Occupancy, specifically chapter 14 on species co-occupancy. I have two questions that I hope could be answered here even though I know this group is about the unmarked package. 

1. What parametrization method does unmarked uses for the occuMulti function? 

2. The co-occupancy model states that species A should be the dominant species (I assume in terms of behavior and not the one suspected to be the most abundant one). So my question is what happens to the model if I switch species and use the non-dominant as species A? The reason I ask is because I am working with a two-species model and even though one of the species is considered to be more dominant, I have some areas where I have few recaptures of this dominant species and lots of the other species which is supposed to be the non-dominant between the two. 

Thanks

Gabby Palomo

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Dominant species in two species co-occupancy model in MacKenzie et al. 2018
parts:
Hi Gabby,

occuMulti is built off of Rota et al.'s 2016 paper  "a multispecies occupancy model for two or more interacting species "(ME&E 7:1164-1173)--actually, this model doesn't assume dominant/subordinate species, so as long as you keep track of which is which, the co-occurrence estimates should be the same (I think?).


John

messages.author: bd00314644d53a96
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Dominant species in two species co-occupancy model in MacKenzie et al. 2018
parts:
Hi Gabriela,
1.As John says, the unmarked model is that of Rota et al 2016, in wich a priori no dominance of any specie is assumed over the other.
 2. The model you refer to is the reparameterization of Richmond et al 2010 which assumes one species is dominant over another, that is, species A influences the observational or ecological process of species B (eg, the wolves affect psi and p of coyotes). As this is not always true in nature, it is good to know about the ecology of both species, besides taking into account that this model only works for the interaction of two species.
The fact of having a greater number of detections (or as you said "recaptures") of the subordinate specie (B) in some areas is perfect, the objective of these models is to determine what influence the change in detection or occupation. Is it due to species A ?, the environment (covariates) ?, or both situations ?.

My English is very rough so I hope you understand me.

regards

parts:
Hi all,

sorry to chime in here with some pedantry: better to say "the model of Richmond et al. and that of Waddle et al.". That's another one of those many examples were the same thing, or almost, was invented simultaneously. These authors describe almost the same, conditional, model with directional dependence of occurrence and detection, published in the same year, same journal (EcoApps). Can't be done in unmarked, but in program PRESENCE (and probably in MARK, too) and of course easy in BUGS.

Best regards  ---- Marc
